'''Susan McKenna-Lawlor''' (born 3 March 1935) is an Irish [[astrophysics|astrophysicist]]. She is an emeritus professor of experimental physics at [[Maynooth University]], having formally retired in 2000.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Day |first=Asteroid |date=2018-06-04 |title=Susan McKenna-Lawlor |url=https://asteroidday.org/people/susan-mckenna-lawlor/ |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=Asteroid Day |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
McKenna-Lawlor was born in Dublin on 3 March 1935. She studied experimental physics at [[University College Dublin]] (BSc 1956, MSc 1959, PhD 1976).<ref name="SR"/> She was a research assistant at the [[Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies]] between 1957 and 1966.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Grace|first=Anne|title=McKenna-Lawlor Susan (Prof.) – DIAS|url=https://www.dias.ie/2013/11/11/mckenna-lawlor-susan-prof/|access-date=6 June 2020|language=en-US}}</ref> Her 1976 UCD doctotral dissertation on ''"A detailed study of phenomena attending the disk passage of an exceptionally active solar region July 07–21, 1959''" was completed under [[Thomas E. Nevin]], based on work originally suggested by [[Mervyn A. Ellison]] of the [[Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies]], and partially completed by McKenna at the University of Michigan.<ref>[https://larouchepub.com/eiw/public/2003/eirv30n47-20031205/eirv30n47-20031205_010-a_brightly_shining_star_susan_mc.pdf ‘A Brightly Shining Star’: Susan McKenna-Lawlor] 
Executive Intelligence Review:Science & Technology, Vol 30, #47, 5 December 2003</ref>

Following her marriage, McKenna-Lawlor became a lecturer in the Department of Experimental Physics at [[St. Patrick's College, Maynooth]] in the early 1970s.<ref>[https://maynoothcollege.ie/files/images/Kalendarium-Chapters-X-Appointments-1795-to-date.pdf Chapter X Appointments 1795 to date] Kalendarium, St. Patrick's College, Maynooth.</ref>  In 1986 she was appointed professor, and she retired from Maynooth in 2000.<ref name=":0" />

==Space Technology Ireland Ltd==
In 1986, she founded the space instrumentation company Space Technology Ireland Ltd (STIL) with venture capitalist [[Dermot Desmond]]. STIL manufactures instruments for space missions where Mckenna serves as the managing director.<ref name=musml>[https://www.maynoothuniversity.ie/people/susan-mckenna-lawlor McKenna-Lawlor]</ref>

== Research and career ==
McKenna-Lawlor was the principal investigator for the Energetic Particle Analyser (EPA) instrument on the [[European Space Agency]] (ESA) [[Giotto (spacecraft)|Giotto]] mission.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ESA Science & Technology - Mission Team|url=https://sci.esa.int/web/giotto/-/31719-mission-team|access-date=5 June 2020|website=sci.esa.int}}</ref> The European Space Agency Solar System working group initially rejected the instrument, before reinstating it in the first half of 1981.<ref name=calder46>{{cite book |last=Calder |first=Nigel |title=Giotto to the Comets |publisher=Presswork |publication-place=London |date=1992 |isbn=0-9520115-0-6 |pages=46–51}}</ref>

McKenna-Lawlor led an international team of scientists in building a particle detector capable of detecting energies between 30 kiloelectronvolts and several megaelectronvolts for the Soviet Union's [[Phobos program|Phobos]] spacecraft in 1988.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=McKenna-Lawlor|first=Susan M. P.|date=September 1989|title=The SLED instrument on the PHOBOS Mission to Mars and its Moons|journal= Irish Astronomical Journal|language=en|volume=19|pages=72|bibcode=1989IrAJ...19...72M|issn=0021-1052}}</ref> The success of the detector led Soviet scientists to ask her to contribute a similar device for their 1994 Mars mission.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1RCzEaxzsbYC&q=susan%20mckenna%20lawlor&pg=PA34 |title=Probe reveals Mars may have radiation belts|journal=New Scientist|date=11 March 1989|last=Henbest|first=Nigel|volume=121|page=34|bibcode=1989NewSc.121...34H}}</ref>

McKenna-Lawlor was a co-investigator for the experiment RAPID on board the [[European Space Agency]] (ESA) [[Cluster II (spacecraft)|Cluster]] mission.<ref>{{Citation|last1=Escoubet|first1=C. P.|chapter=Directory of Cluster Community Members (24 May 1996)|date=1997|title=The Cluster and Phoenix Missions|pages=639–658|editor-last=Escoubet|editor-first=C. P.|publisher=Springer Netherlands|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-94-011-5666-0_21|isbn=978-94-011-5666-0|last2=Russell|first2=C. T.|last3=Schmidt|first3=R.|editor2-last=Russell|editor2-first=C. T.|editor3-last=Schmidt|editor3-first=R.}}</ref> She also developed instruments to monitor the solar wind on Mars for the ESA [[Mars Express]] mission.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Barabash|first1=S.|last2=Lundin|first2=R.|last3=Andersson|first3=H.|last4=Gimholt|first4=J.|last5=Holmström|first5=M.|last6=Norberg|first6=O.|last7=Yamauchi|first7=M.|last8=Asamura|first8=K.|last9=Coates|first9=A. J.|last10=Linder|first10=D. R.|last11=Kataria|first11=D. O.|date=August 2004|chapter=ASPERA-3: analyser of space plasmas and energetic ions for Mars Express|title= Mars Express: The Scientific Payload|series=Proceedings of the ESA Workshop on Aerospace EMC |journal=<!-- -->|editor1=Andrew Wilson |editor2=Agustin Chicarro |publisher=ESA Publications Division|language=en|volume=1240|pages=121–139|bibcode=2004ESASP1240..121B|issn=1609-042X|isbn=92-9092-556-6}}</ref>

STIL designed the onboard Electrical Support System processor unit for the ''[[Rosetta (spacecraft)|Rosetta]]'' spacecraft. McKenna-Lawlor also represented Ireland on the Steering Board of the Rosetta's [[Philae (spacecraft)|Philae]] lander that landed on comet [[67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko]].<ref name="SR">{{cite news|title=Irish scientist's role in comet-chasing Rosetta mission|url=https://www.siliconrepublic.com/innovation/2014/01/17/irish-scientists-role-in-comet-chasing-rosetta-mission |last=O'Connell|first=Claire|date=17 January 2014|work=Silicon Republic}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
McKenna-Lawlor was a winner of the [[List of People of the Year Award winners|Rehab People of the Year Award]] in 1986. She was elected to the [[International Academy of Astronautics]], and in 2005 she received an honorary DSc from the [[University of Ulster]] for her contributions to astrophysics.<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Academy of Astronautics|url=https://iaaweb.org/content/view/9/53/|access-date=6 June 2020|website=iaaweb.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Honorary graduates|url=https://www.ulster.ac.uk/about/governance/secretariat/honorary-graduates|access-date=6 June 2020|website=www.ulster.ac.uk|language=en}}</ref>

She was a member of the [[National University of Ireland]] Senate and of [[Maynooth University]]'s Governing Authority.<ref name=musml />
